description: An an app that installs Sidestore on iOS 27, fully on-device

latest_release.name: v1.7.0
latest_release.body:
### Added
- **Turkish.** Pick Türkçe in Settings › Language. Thanks to Mr3242-Scripter (#111).
- **A nudge to update to iOS 27 at setup** on devices that can run it: on iOS 27 the iPhone pairs with itself, no computer needed.

### Changed
- **Side by Side goes step by step** and can now install SideStore and LiveContainer + SideStore too (Stable or Nightly), each set up with the pairing file on the other iPhone.
- **Your Apple ID session and pairing stay on this iPhone:** private files are left out of backups, and the saved password is kept in the Keychain for this device only. After restoring a backup, sign in and pair again.

### Fixed
- Keys and passwords no longer end up in the activity log or problem reports.
- Side by Side no longer keeps the other person's signing key on your iPhone.
- A stalled pairing can be cancelled, and gives up by itself.
- Two sign-ins running at once no longer share one 2FA code; the number pad comes back after a wrong code.
- Local Network turned off is noticed in about two seconds instead of a minute.
- Pairing keeps going through a call, Siri, an alarm or AirPods connecting.
- The app stays smooth while the activity log fills.

# SideInstaller **Install SideStore and LiveContainer directly on your iPhone. No PC required.** [![Install](https://img.shields.io/badge/Install-SideInstaller-2ea44f?style=for-the-badge)](https://sideinstaller.net/) [![Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-1.7.0-blue?style=for-the-badge)](CHANGELOG.md) [![Platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-iOS-lightgrey?style=for-the-badge&logo=apple)](#requirements) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Custom-orange?style=for-the-badge)](LICENSE.md)
--- > [!CAUTION] > **Only install SideInstaller from the official source.** > > This project is open source, which means anyone can fork the code, insert a credential stealer that > uploads your Apple ID and password to their own server, rebuild it, and redistribute it under the same > name and icon. A malicious fork looks identical to the real app from the outside. > > The **only** builds I publish are: > - **Website:** https://sideinstaller.net/ > - **Repository:** https://github.com/FrizzleM/SideInstaller > > Do not install SideInstaller from any other site, AltStore source, Telegram channel, Discord server, > app repo, or mirror, no matter how official it looks. Redistributing my builds without explicit consent is also prohibited by > the [license](LICENSE.md). > > There is a fake site called “sideinstaller.com”. This site is **not legit**, and is likely providing malware. Please make sure > you only download from the **official sources** listed above. --- ## What it is SideStore and LiveContainer are currently the best way to sideload on iOS. However, there's one big problem: installing them requires a PC, which many people don't have. That's why I made SideInstaller, a free and open-source iOS app that installs them directly on your iPhone, no PC required. SideInstaller handles the entire setup process on-device. It takes care of the pairing, provisioning, and installation steps that normally force you to plug into a computer and run desktop tools, all from a single app running on the phone itself. Once it's done, you get a fully working SideStore and LiveContainer setup ready to sideload your own apps. The whole thing is built to be simple. There's no complicated configuration, no command line, and no need to understand how any of the underlying machinery works. You just open the app, follow a few steps, and let it do the rest. For anyone who's ever wanted to sideload but didn't own a Mac or PC, this removes the biggest barrier to getting started. And because it's open source, you don't have to take my word for any of it. The full code is available for anyone to read, audit, or contribute to, so you can see exactly what's running on your device. ## Requirements - An iPhone or iPad on iOS 27+ (iOS 17.4+ with a pairing file made on a computer; from iOS 26.4, a [remote pairing one](#ios-264-to-26x-a-remote-pairing-file)) - Wi-Fi (first time only) - Your Apple account credentials (not collected) ## How to use it 1. Open [the official install page](https://sideinstaller.net/) and install the app using any of the certificates. 2. Once it's installed, open it. 3. Connect the device to LocalDevVPN (or any alternative) 4. Log in with your Apple account credentials. 5. Tap **Install SideStore** or **Install SideStore + LiveContainer**. 6. Wait while your selection installs. 7. That's it. No PC and no extra steps required. ### Without a certificate: from the iPhone itself No install page, no certificate, no computer: two free App Store apps put SideInstaller on the iPhone they run on, signed with your own Apple account. iOS 27 or later, Developer Mode on, Wi-Fi and LocalDevVPN connected. 1. Install [rootshell](https://apps.apple.com/app/rootshell-local-terminal-ssh/id6755794662) and [Open Minis](https://apps.apple.com/app/id6759188481) from the App Store. 2. In rootshell, turn on **Settings › Location Diary Mode › Session Only**, then in its local shell run, one line at a time: ```sh curl -fsSLO https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FrizzleM/SideInstaller/main/rootshell/bin/siboot-pair.wasm ifconfig en0 > ifconfig.txt ./siboot-pair.wasm ``` One line at a time: rootshell doesn't run the three joined with `&&`. Open **Settings › Privacy & Security › Developer Mode**, scroll down, tap **Pair with siboot**, and enter your passcode and the code rootshell shows. Leave rootshell running. (If it finds no address, run `./siboot-pair.wasm` followed by the IP address in **Settings › Wi-Fi › ⓘ**.) 3. In Minis's terminal (**Minis › Settings › Terminal**), run: ```sh wget -qO- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FrizzleM/SideInstaller/main/minis/install.sh | sh ``` Type the transfer code rootshell shows, then your Apple account email, password and code. How and why it works: [`minis/`](minis/) and [`rootshell/`](rootshell/). ### Links SideInstaller opens three kinds of `sideinstaller://` link, and asks before acting on any of them: - `sideinstaller://install?url=` downloads the IPA as the custom .ipa and installs it, for one-tap installs from a website. - `sideinstaller://pairingFile?data=` imports a pairing file. SideStore sends one back when asked with `sidestore://pairing?urlname=sideinstaller`, which is what **Get it from SideStore** on the Pairing file card does. - `sideinstaller://certificate?data=&password=` makes SideInstaller sign with that certificate from then on, once Apple lists it among your Apple ID's certificates. **Use SideStore's certificate** (on the “A certificate already exists” popup and the Certificates page) asks SideStore for its own with `sidestore://certificate?callback_template=sideinstaller://certificate?data=$(BASE64_CERT)&password=$(PASSWORD)` (percent-encoded), so a free Apple ID's one certificate serves both apps. That reply is the one link that doesn't ask again: SideStore has just asked whether to export it. Discord and most chat apps only make `https://` links tappable, so to post an install link there use `https://sideinstaller.net/open.html?url=`. That page shows where the IPA downloads from and hands it to `sideinstaller://install`, with a button for when iOS doesn't open the app on its own. ## Compatibility | iOS | Is it compatible? | | --- | --- | | 27+ | ✅ Yes | | 26.4 - 26.7 | ⚠️ Yes, but [a remote pairing file is needed](#ios-264-to-26x-a-remote-pairing-file), and that requires a PC | | 17.4 - 26.3 | ⚠️ Yes, but [a pairing file is needed](https://docs.sidestore.io/docs/advanced/alternative#pairing), and that requires a PC | | <17.4 | ❌ No | ### iOS 26.4 to 26.x: a remote pairing file Since iOS 26.4, the iPhone hangs up on lockdown pairing files (from jitterbugpair, `pymobiledevice3 lockdown pair`, or idevice_pair's **Lockdown**) as soon as they connect through LocalDevVPN, so they can't be used on the iPhone any more, however new. A remote pairing (RPPairing) file still works: 1. On a Mac, Windows PC or Linux computer, open [idevice_pair](https://github.com/jkcoxson/idevice_pair/releases/latest) and plug the iPhone in. Tap **Trust** if it asks. 2. Pick the iPhone, choose **Remote pairing**, click **Create**, and keep the iPhone unlocked until it's done. 3. Click **Save to file…** and send the file to the iPhone by AirDrop, iCloud Drive or a cable. 4. In SideInstaller, tap **Import pairing file** (or **Replace**) and pick it. A pairing file exported from [iLoader](https://github.com/nab138/iloader) (**Manage Pairing File** › **Export**) holds both kinds and works too. ## Is SideInstaller safe? SideInstaller is built with safety and privacy in mind. The app is fully local and open source, which means anyone can inspect exactly what it does. **Your Apple credentials never leave your device.** They're used locally, only to sign and install your apps, and are never transmitted, logged, or collected in any way. **No server, no analytics, no account.** Nothing is collected and there's nothing to sign up for. **Fully auditable.** Every line of it can be verified in the source code. > [!WARNING] > All of the above is true of **this** repository and the builds published from it. It is **not** a guarantee > that applies to forks, re-signed IPAs, or copies you find elsewhere, those can be modified to steal the > Apple ID you type into them. If you didn't get it from > https://sideinstaller.net/, don't trust it with your > credentials. ## Project layout | Path | What's in it | | :-- | :-- | | `ios-app/` | The SwiftUI app — UI, install engine, certificate handling, translations | | `ios-live-activity/` | The widget extension that draws the pairing code in the Dynamic Island and on the Lock Screen | | `ios-tests/` | The app's unit tests (`SideInstallerTests`) | | `rust-core/` | Rust core compiled into `SideInstallerFFI.xcframework` | | `scripts/` | Build, check and release scripts | | `minis/` | siboot for Open Minis: installs SideInstaller from the iPhone it runs on, no computer | | `rootshell/` | siboot's pairing step for rootshell, so the iPhone pairs with itself from an App Store app | | `.github/` | Workflows that check pull requests, build the unsigned IPA, publish it as a release and hand it to the signer | Signed builds and the install page live in [FrizzleM/SideInstaller-Signed](https://github.com/FrizzleM/SideInstaller-Signed): it signs each release's IPA with every certificate, attaches the signed IPAs to a release of its own and deploys [sideinstaller.net](https://sideinstaller.net/). No IPA is ever committed to either repository. ## Contributing Issues and pull requests are welcome. If you're reporting a bug, please include your iOS version, the app version, and the step where it failed. Every pull request is checked by the `checks` workflow: the Rust tests and clippy, a simulator build with the app's unit tests, and the translations (a string added to the app needs an entry in each `ios-app/*Strings.swift`). The same checks run on a Mac with `scripts/test-rust.sh`, `scripts/check-ios.sh` (in a clean clone, since it generates the Xcode project) and `scripts/check_translations.py`. ## License See [LICENSE.md](LICENSE.md). In short: you may read, modify, and share the **source**, with attribution, for non-commercial purposes. Redistributing the official builds (IPAs) or monetizing the project in any form requires written permission.
